_README: THE CHARACTER LOCK. One place that says what each character looks like, so two pictures of the same
person cannot disagree. Nothing else in this repo is allowed to describe a locked character in prose.
HOW IT IS USED
docs/prompts.md writes {CafeWalker} inside a '> ' prompt line. tools/gen_images.py replaces that token
with 'prompt' below before it sends anything to the model, so every picture gets the SAME words.
tools/char_lock_check.py fails if a prompt writes a locked character out by hand instead.
WHY IT EXISTS
Fri Nov 13: the title card, the 'to be continued' card and the itch.io cover each drew the main
character's apron differently - a crossed X-back, a plain shirt back, and a bib with no neck strap at
all. Three pictures, three aprons. A player reads that as AI slop, correctly.
THE RULE FOR CHANGING ONE
'sheet' is the drawing the rigged 3D model was made from. It is the truth. If you change a lock you are
saying the MODEL is wrong, so the model gets remade too - never change a lock just to match a picture
that came out differently.
SHORT FORM: write {CafeWalker:short} when the character is small or far away in the frame. It is the
same lock, shortened to the details that still read at that size - the apron's single neck loop and bare
back are kept in BOTH forms, because that is the detail that drifted.
'sheet_prompts' are the prompt codes that DREW the canonical sheet. They are the lock's own source,
so char_lock_check.py lets them describe the character in their own words. Nothing else may.
Changing one of those prompts means redrawing the sheet AND remaking the rigged model.
CAMERA ANGLE IS PART OF THE LOCK. If the detail that drifts lives on a surface the camera cannot see, the
model will invent that surface. The apron's single neck loop is the clearest example: drawn from directly
behind, the model reaches for the cross-back apron it has seen a thousand times and the words do not stop
it (three takes, three cross-backs). Pose a locked character so the distinguishing detail is IN FRAME -
side or three-quarter for this apron - or use --lock-ref and hand the model the sheet itself.

CafeWalker.role: the player character, a coffee shop worker
CafeWalker.prompt: a slim young man of about twenty-five with short messy straight black hair falling over his forehead and covering the tops of his ears, a thin calm tired face, wearing a khaki brown long-sleeve collared button shirt with the sleeves pushed up to just below the elbow and the collar open, over it a plain dark green bib apron that hangs over one single strap looped around the back of his neck leaving his shirt back completely bare with no crossed straps, one square patch pocket on the chest of the bib, the long apron waist ties brought round and knotted in a simple bow at the front of his waist just under the bib, a pale grey bar towel tucked into the waist tie at his left hip, the apron reaching below his knees, loose charcoal grey trousers and grey canvas low-top sneakers with white toe caps
CafeWalker.prompt_short: a slim young man with short messy black hair, wearing a khaki brown long-sleeve shirt with the sleeves pushed up and a dark green bib apron that hangs from one single strap looped behind his neck, leaving his shirt back completely bare with no crossed straps and the apron ties knotted at the front
invariants: ONE neck loop. The apron goes over the head on a single strap. The back is bare shirt.
NEVER crossed straps, NEVER an X on the back, NEVER a two-strap cross-back apron.
The bib has one square chest pocket.
The waist ties knot at the FRONT, in a bow, under the bib. Not at the back.
A pale grey bar towel hangs at his left hip.
Sleeves are pushed up to below the elbow, forearms bare. Shirt is khaki brown, never cream.
The apron is below the knee, not a short waist apron.
CafeWalker.never: cream shirt, white shirt, crossed apron straps, cross-back apron, X straps on the back, apron with no neck strap, short waist apron, bare chest, tie, waistcoat, glasses, beard, blond hair, hat

CafeCoworker.prompt: a young woman of about twenty-four with dark brown hair pulled back into a short high ponytail and a loose fringe, wearing a pure white short-sleeve collared shirt and over it a plain teal bib apron on one single strap looped around the back of her neck leaving her shirt back bare with no crossed straps, the apron waist ties knotted in a bow at the front of her waist, dark navy trousers and plain black flat shoes
CafeCoworker.prompt_short: a young woman with dark brown hair in a short high ponytail, wearing a pure white short-sleeve shirt and a teal bib apron on one single neck strap with a bare shirt back
invariants: ONE neck loop, bare shirt back, ties knotted at the FRONT - the same apron pattern as CafeWalker, different colour.
Her shirt is PURE WHITE, never cream, never beige, never tan.
Short high ponytail, never loose hair, never a bun.
Her apron is teal. It is not the player's dark green.
CafeCoworker.never: cream shirt, beige shirt, tan shirt, crossed apron straps, cross-back apron, loose hair, bun, green apron, long sleeves

CrashDriver.role: boss 1, already dead in the wrecked car; touching him grants Freeze Frame
CrashDriver.prompt: a heavy-set man in his fifties with short grey-streaked dark hair, wearing a worn dark brown leather jacket over a black shirt, dark brown trousers and heavy black boots
CrashDriver.prompt_short: a heavy middle-aged man in a worn brown leather jacket and dark trousers
invariants: Brown leather jacket, never black leather.
No blood and no wounds anywhere - the game is rated 13+.
CrashDriver.never: blood, wound, gore, injury, black leather jacket, young man, uniform, helmet
